answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its votes count. A knoll of fresh accounts adds influence only if the attacker funds each one; if those accounts certify fake work, participants can challenge the claim against signed logs and slash the stake. Creating identities is cheap, but buying and risking capital per identity is not. A terrace of accounts may look large, yet the tide of influence is bounded by the attacker’s funds.
